source: ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline, effective 2024-04-15 (Public Use Only)

items.1.1: Understand, adhere to, and promote professional ethics
items.1.2.1: Confidentiality, integrity, and availability, authenticity, and nonrepudiation (5 Pillars of Information Security)
items.1.3: Evaluate, apply, and sustain security governance principles
items.1.3.1: Alignment of the security function to business strategy, goals, mission, and objectives
items.1.3.2: Organizational processes (e.g., acquisitions, divestitures, governance committees)
items.1.3.4: Security control frameworks (e.g., International Organization for Standardization (ISO), National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Control Objectives for Information and Related Technology (COBIT), Sherwood Applied Business Security Architecture (SABSA), Payment Card Industry (PCI), Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP))
items.1.4: Understand legal, regulatory, and compliance issues that pertain to information security in a holistic context
items.1.4.5: Issues related to privacy (e.g., General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), California Consumer Privacy Act, Personal Information Protection Law, Protection of Personal Information Act)
items.1.4.6: Contractual, legal, industry standards, and regulatory requirements
items.1.5: Understand requirements for investigation types (i.e., administrative, criminal, civil, regulatory, industry standards)
items.1.6: Develop, document, and implement security policy, standards, procedures, and guidelines
items.1.7: Identify, analyze, assess, prioritize, and implement Business Continuity (BC) requirements
items.1.8: Contribute to and enforce personnel security policies and procedures
items.1.8.2: Employment agreements and policy driven requirements
items.1.8.4: Vendor, consultant, and contractor agreements and controls
items.1.9: Understand and apply risk management concepts
items.1.9.3: Risk response and treatment (e.g., cybersecurity insurance)
items.1.9.4: Applicable types of controls (e.g., preventive, detection, corrective)
items.1.9.9: Risk frameworks (e.g., International Organization for Standardization (ISO), National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Control Objectives for Information and Related Technology (COBIT), Sherwood Applied Business Security Architecture (SABSA), Payment Card Industry (PCI))
items.1.10: Understand and apply threat modeling concepts and methodologies
items.1.11: Apply supply chain risk management (SCRM) concepts
items.1.11.1: Risks associated with the acquisition of products and services from suppliers and providers (e.g., product tampering, counterfeits, implants)
items.1.11.2: Risk mitigations (e.g., third-party assessment and monitoring, minimum security requirements, service level requirements, silicon root of trust, physically unclonable function, software bill of materials)
items.1.12: Establish and maintain a security awareness, education, and training program
items.1.12.1: Methods and techniques to increase awareness and training (e.g., social engineering, phishing, security champions, gamification)
items.1.12.2: Periodic content reviews to include emerging technologies and trends (e.g., cryptocurrency, artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain)
items.2.1: Identify and classify information and assets
items.2.2: Establish information and asset handling requirements
items.2.4.1: Data roles (i.e., owners, controllers, custodians, processors, users/subjects)
items.2.5: Ensure appropriate asset retention (e.g., End of Life (EOL), End of Support)
items.2.6: Determine data security controls and compliance requirements
items.2.6.1: Data states (e.g., in use, in transit, at rest)
items.2.6.4: Data protection methods (e.g., Digital Rights Management (DRM), data loss prevention (DLP), cloud access security broker (CASB))
items.3.1: Research, implement, and manage engineering processes using secure design principles
items.3.1.8: Zero trust or trust but verify
items.3.2: Understand the fundamental concepts of security models (e.g., Biba, Star Model, Bell-LaPadula)
items.3.3: Select controls based upon systems security requirements
items.3.4: Understand security capabilities of Information Systems (e.g., memory protection, Trusted Platform Module (TPM), encryption/decryption)
items.3.5: Assess and mitigate the vulnerabilities of security architectures, designs, and solution elements
items.3.5.6: Cloud-based systems (e.g., Software as a Service (SaaS), Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS))
items.3.6.1: Cryptographic life cycle (e.g., keys, algorithm selection)
items.3.6.2: Cryptographic methods (e.g., symmetric, asymmetric, elliptic curves, quantum)
items.3.6.3: Public key infrastructure (PKI) (e.g., quantum key distribution)
items.3.6.5: Digital signatures and digital certificates (e.g., non-repudiation, integrity)
items.3.8: Apply security principles to site and facility design
items.3.9: Design site and facility security controls
items.3.9.6: Utilities and Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC)
items.4.1: Apply secure design principles in network architectures
items.4.1.1: Open System Interconnection (OSI) and Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol (TCP/IP) models
items.4.1.2: Internet Protocol (IP) version 4 and 6 (IPv6) (e.g., unicast, broadcast, multicast, anycast)
items.4.1.3: Secure protocols (e.g., Internet Protocol Security (IPSec), Secure Shell (SSH), Secure Sockets Layer (SSL)/Transport Layer Security (TLS))
items.4.1.5: Converged protocols (e.g., Internet Small Computer Systems Interface (iSCSI), Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP), InfiniBand over Ethernet, Compute Express Link)
items.4.1.6: Transport architecture (e.g., topology, data/control/management plane, cut-through/store-and-forward)
items.4.1.7: Performance metrics (e.g., bandwidth, latency, jitter, throughput, signal-to-noise ratio)
items.4.1.10: Logical segmentation (e.g., virtual local area networks (VLANs), virtual private networks (VPNs), virtual routing and forwarding, virtual domain)
items.4.1.11: Micro-segmentation (e.g., network overlays/encapsulation; distributed firewalls, routers, intrusion detection system (IDS)/intrusion prevention system (IPS), zero trust)
items.4.1.13: Wireless networks (e.g., Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, Zigbee, satellite)
items.4.1.16: Software defined networks (SDN), (e.g., application programming interface (API), Software-Defined Wide-Area Network, network functions virtualization)
items.4.1.18: Monitoring and management (e.g., network observability, traffic flow/shaping, capacity management, fault detection and handling)
items.4.2.1: Operation of infrastructure (e.g., redundant power, warranty, support)
items.4.2.2: Transmission media (e.g., physical security of media, signal propagation quality)
items.4.2.3: Network Access Control (NAC) systems (e.g., physical, and virtual solutions)
items.4.3: Implement secure communication channels according to design
items.4.3.1: Voice, video, and collaboration (e.g., conferencing, Zoom rooms)
items.4.3.4: Third-party connectivity (e.g., telecom providers, hardware support)
items.5.1: Control physical and logical access to assets
items.5.2: Design identification and authentication strategy (e.g., people, devices, and services)
items.5.2.2: Authentication, Authorization and Accounting (AAA) (e.g., multi-factor authentication (MFA), password-less authentication)
items.5.2.4: Registration, proofing, and establishment of identity
items.5.3: Federated identity with a third-party service
items.5.4.7: Access policy enforcement (e.g., policy decision point, policy enforcement point)
items.5.5: Manage the identity and access provisioning lifecycle
items.5.5.1: Account access review (e.g., user, system, service)
items.5.5.2: Provisioning and deprovisioning (e.g., on/off boarding and transfers)
items.5.5.3: Role definition and transition (e.g., people assigned to new roles)
items.5.5.4: Privilege escalation (e.g., use of sudo, auditing its use)
items.6.1: Design and validate assessment, test, and audit strategies
items.6.2.2: Penetration testing (e.g., red, blue, and/or purple team exercises)
items.6.2.8: Interface testing (e.g., user interface, network interface, application programming interface (API))
items.6.3: Collect security process data (e.g., technical, and administrative)
items.6.4: Analyze test output and generate report
items.7.1.4: Digital forensics tools, tactics, and procedures
items.7.1.5: Artifacts (e.g., data, computer, network, mobile device)
items.7.2.7: Threat intelligence (e.g., threat feeds, threat hunting)
items.7.3: Perform configuration management (CM) (e.g., provisioning, baselining, automation)
items.7.7: Operate and maintain detection and preventative measures
items.7.7.1: Firewalls (e.g., next generation, web application, network)
items.7.7.2: Intrusion detection systems (IDS) and intrusion prevention systems (IPS)
items.7.7.8: Machine learning and artificial intelligence (AI) based tools
items.7.8: Implement and support patch and vulnerability management
items.7.9: Understand and participate in change management processes
items.7.10.1: Backup storage strategies (e.g., cloud storage, onsite, offsite)
items.7.10.2: Recovery site strategies (e.g., cold vs. hot, resource capacity agreements)
items.7.10.4: System resilience, high availability (HA), Quality of Service (QoS), and fault tolerance
items.7.13: Participate in Business Continuity (BC) planning and exercises
items.7.15: Address personnel safety and security concerns
items.7.15.2: Security training and awareness (e.g., insider threat, social media impacts, two-factor authentication (2FA) fatigue)
items.8.1: Understand and integrate security in the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC)
items.8.1.1: Development methodologies (e.g., Agile, Waterfall, DevOps, DevSecOps, Scaled Agile Framework)
items.8.1.2: Maturity models (e.g., Capability Maturity Model (CMM), Software Assurance Maturity Model (SAMM))
items.8.2: Identify and apply security controls in software development ecosystems
items.8.2.9: Application security testing (e.g., static application security testing (SAST), dynamic application security testing (DAST), software composition analysis, Interactive Application Security Test (IAST))
items.8.3: Assess the effectiveness of software security
items.8.4: Assess security impact of acquired software
items.8.4.5: Cloud services (e.g., Software as a Service (SaaS), Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS))
items.8.5: Define and apply secure coding guidelines and standards
items.8.5.1: Security weaknesses and vulnerabilities at the source-code level
